_about: How each receiver compresses audio and waterfall, as its code and docs say at the pinned version. Sources are the research reports kept with the plan (report-nova-phantom-vertex.md, report-owrx-pa3fwm-ka9q-uber.md) and the files named. bins_per_row is what the listener's socket carries per waterfall row at the lab's settings; null where it depends on the viewport and was not read from the protocol. Measured rates are in bench/runs/*/summary-compression.*.

audio.codec: NAC3, FernSDR's own MDCT transform codec
audio.notes: quantisation noise held a set margin under the channel noise it measures (docs/CODEC.md)

waterfall.codec: WFC5: dB levels rounded to 1 dB (at most 0.5 dB error) or, as the page asks in Low and Balanced, 2 dB (at most 1 dB), range -200 to +100 dB; each residual against the bin to the left coded as binary decisions with adaptive probabilities, in contexts from the row above, through LZMA's range coder; a key row every 24 rows
waterfall.lossy_part: only the level rounding; the range coder reconstructs the rounded levels exactly
waterfall.notes: row width follows the viewport; FFT bins are mapped to pixels by peak selection so narrow carriers stay visible; zoomed in, native FFT bins are sent. In the lab the page asked for wfc5 with step_db 2; pages without WFC5 get WFC4.

waterfall.codec: 8-bit dB rows in CBOR, zstd stream
waterfall.notes: lossy only by the 8-bit quantisation; zstd itself is lossless

audio.codec: FLAC at 8 bits a sample in CBOR
audio.notes: samples cut to 8 bits, then lossless FLAC

audio.codec: FLAC of 16-bit samples (default); Opus for C-QUAM
the PA3FWM WebSDR audio format (tag-byte frames)

audio.notes: closed source; FAQ: about 100 kbit/s a user with one slow waterfall

waterfall.codec: PA3FWM waterfall format 9/10, 1.5 to 2.3 bits a pixel

audio.codec: IMA ADPCM, 4 bits a sample at 12 kHz
IMA ADPCM, 4 bits a sample at 12 kHz
Opus (default) over RTP; 16-bit PCM at 12 kHz optional

waterfall.codec: one byte a bin, uncompressed, after a float header
waterfall.notes: lossy only by the 8-bit quantisation; 10 rows a second
one byte a bin; 10 rows a second
